The structure of Mg12Fe4Co2 (reduced formula Mg6Fe2Co) crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Amm2 (No. 38), with 18 atoms in the unit cell distributed over six independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows all Co, Fe, and Mg centers adopt a close-packed-like local arrangement with 12 geometric neighbors each, with Mg–Mg coordination dominating the environments. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 18 sites, and validated polyhedron-sharing analysis identifies corner-, edge-, and face-sharing among 12-vertex Mg-centered coordination polyhedra.
